title: Some ocean views are a lifeboat, in daylight.
subtitle: The word *obstructed* is doing a great deal of quiet work on that booking page.

text: An ocean view is a promise about a window, not about a view.
sub: The category means glass in the hull. It does not mean the sea is on the other side of it. What is on the other side may be davits, a steel rail, or a tender in its cradle.

items.head: Obstructed
items.body: Something structural sits between you and the water. The line has told you, in one word, and hoped you'd skim.

items.head: Partially obstructed
items.body: Usually the corner of the same object. Sometimes genuinely fine, and sometimes the whole frame.

items.head: Fully obstructed, reduced fare
items.body: Honest, and occasionally the smartest cabin on the ship — if you were never going to look out.

quote: A window you keep covered is an interior cabin you overpaid for.

text: Buy the obstruction on purpose, or don't buy the window.
sub: If you only sleep in the cabin, take the obstructed fare and put the difference into the itinerary. If the view is the point, insist on a category with no qualifier attached to it.

title: Send this to whoever books the cabins.
body: Or send me the category code you've been quoted. I'll tell you what is actually outside that glass before your deposit becomes non-refundable.
